essence: Sky-formed self, directions uncovered: own form shows.
Pierced limb, awareness yoked: spotless going in Bhairava.
Inner-making not in me: fancies fall by absence.
Māyā deluding: counted realities never stand apart.
Seen desire led to calm: dissolves where it arose.
Desire unarisen: truly He-I, dissolved, that-minded.
Either desire or knowing: undivided mind sees meaning.
Causeless knowing, anyone's nothing: thus becoming Śiva.
No bodily distinction: contemplating all, world-conqueror.

rasa.dominant: adbhuta tipping into śānta (wonder at identity unmade)
rasa.justification: The He-I realization is the text's climactic wonder, but its grammar is subtraction — no inner-making, no separateness, no anyone — so wonder arrives as emptiness being said.

sections.SUMMARY: The letter-to-identity block: emission-ending awareness touching eternal brahman; sky-formed self uncovered by directions showing own form; a limb pierced and yoked to spotless going; the denial that anything inner-making is inside me, letting fancies fall by their own absence; māyä named as delusion counting realities that never stand apart; sudden desire led to calm where it arose; desire unarisen revealing He-I, dissolved, that-minded; mind set undivided in either desire or knowing seeing reality's meaning; knowledge turning causeless, no one's, Śiva; and no bodily distinction anywhere — the contemplating one conquers the world.
sections.FUNCTION: Subtracts every inner stake until the identity statement stands with nothing behind it.
sections.KEY TERMS: jñāna (knowing as causeless); antaḥ-karaṇa-denial (no inner-making); māyā (delusion as counting); He-I (tadāsmi / so'ham as subtraction-result); sarva-deha (bodies as distinction-less).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Identity-claims prepare the passions-neutral block (p11); 'world-conqueror' prefigures the fruit-talk later.
sections.BOUNDARY: No claim that one cannot act: distinction-less bodies still conquer worlds — difference denied, function intact.
sections.EXPLANATION: Vowel-precision (emission-ending awareness) makes contact eternal; then sky and directions; then the somatic puncture (a limb pierced with needle, awareness yoked) yielding spotless going. What follows is pure apophasis: the claim that nothing inner-making is inside — so fancies fall not by attack but by absence; māyā is only the counting that cannot keep realities apart; desire must be led (not killed) to dissolve where it arose, and unrisen desire reveals the He-I. In either desire or knowing, undivided mind sees meaning; knowledge without ground, without owner, IS becoming Śiva — and the bodies, distinction-less in all, are what the contemplating person conquers worlds with.
sections.RELATED: So'ham dialectic (cf. v97 '=B9haṃ' byte); māyā as kalana (counting) matches Parātriṃśikā's counting-verse — cross-reference as parallel, not source.
